records.name: Jewish Chorale of Greater Philadelphia (Nashirah)
records.summary: A choir in the Philadelphia region that sings Jewish choral music. You join by audition, and the choir gives concerts through its season.
records.what_you_do: Audition to sing in the choir, or come to one of its concerts. Auditions for the 2026 to 2027 season are open to prospective singers.

schedule.text: Concerts through the 2026 to 2027 season. Auditions are by appointment, in person or online.

cost.text: The site does not show audition or membership costs.

first_step.how: Email manager@nashirah.org to book an audition for the 2026 to 2027 season. Auditions are by appointment, in person or online.
first_step.basis: You must audition by appointment before joining, and the site does not say who may audition or describe a beginner route.
first_step.what_to_expect: Staff email you to confirm an audition time, which can be in person or online. The audition checks sight-reading, tonal memory, rhythm, vocal range, and how even your tone is. The site does not give the audition length, fees, or rehearsal times, so ask when you book.
first_visit_tips: Arrive at least 15 minutes before your confirmed time.
Ask about rehearsal days, fees, and membership terms when you email, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the auditions, performance and about pages. Auditions are by appointment, booked by email, in person or online; the site does not say who may audition, how long it lasts, or what it costs. Rehearsal days and place are not published, and membership terms are not described. Status moved from probably active to active on the June 2026 festival performances listed on the performance page (those concerts were in Prague). Tier 1 listed the same mailing address twice; merged into one entry.

records.name: Logan Square Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Neighbors in Logan Square who meet monthly to talk about zoning, safety, transportation and building plans, then share the group's views with the City and developers. The group has operated for about 50 years.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly board meeting, ask to join a committee (such as zoning, transportation, or planning and design), or join in neighborhood events.

schedule.text: Board meetings on the second Tuesday of each month at 7 pm, at a place that changes around the neighborhood.

locations.label: Monthly board meeting
locations.address: Rotating places in the neighborhood. The July 14, 2026 meeting was at The Chubb Building, 2000 Arch St.

cost.text: The site asks for an annual membership or donation but does not list an amount.

first_step.how: Come to the monthly board meeting on the second Tuesday at 7 pm. The place changes, so check the email list or the events page first. You can join as a member online, or print and mail a form.
first_step.basis: The monthly meeting is open to neighbors and the site explains how to join, but it does not say how a new person gets onto a committee.
first_step.what_to_expect: The board meets once a month, on the second Tuesday at 7 pm, at a place that changes around the neighborhood. Neighbors who live in the area can attend without paying dues, and only dues-paying members vote in the June election. The site does not describe the agenda or how long a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Look up the meeting place before you go, since it changes.
Email info@lsnaphilly.org to ask which committees take new members.
Only dues-paying members can vote, so you can attend first and decide about membership later.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the membership, board meeting, committee, contact and events pages. Two changes need a reviewer's eye. (1) The group's own contact page lists info@lsnaphilly.org as the general address, so the email field now uses it; the tier 1 address wenmoutha@outlook.com came from the City RCO list and is no longer in this record. (2) The homepage lists a block party on September 27, 2026, but the events page does not, so it is not used to date the record. Whether committee meetings are open to the public is not stated, and no dues amount is published. The phone number and contact name are from the City list; the group's site shows no phone.

records.name: Lyra Society
records.summary: A harp nonprofit that teaches harp and helps students with college applications at partner Philadelphia public schools, at no cost to them. Adults can volunteer on its committees and attend public concerts and benefits.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer committee (college guidance, development and marketing, events, finance, technology and website, or the Young Friends group for ages 21 to 65), or attend a public concert or benefit. Students at partner schools take part through the Glissando Program.

schedule.text: Public concerts, showcases and benefits are listed on the events page through the year. Committee meeting times are not stated.

cost.text: Glissando services are free to students at partner schools. Public event prices are not listed on the events page.

first_step.how: Email info@LyraSociety.org with your résumé or LinkedIn profile and the committee you want to join. To see the group first, attend a public concert or benefit listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: Volunteer roles start with an emailed résumé or LinkedIn profile and a committee choice, which is a light application. Public events are open to the public, but many need a ticket or a reservation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each committee has its own job, such as planning fundraisers, managing the budget, or helping students apply to college. The site does not give committee meeting days, times, or places, or how much time a volunteer should expect. A public concert or benefit is a simpler first look at the group, but tickets or reservations are often needed.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for a ticket or reservation before you go.
Name the committee you want in your email, and attach a résumé or LinkedIn profile.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the volunteer, Glissando and events pages. The volunteer page names six committees and the Young Friends group (ages 21 to 65), all joined by email. Glissando is for selected students at partner schools, is free to them, and is not open to the public. The events page lists a June 3, 2026 golf benefit as the newest public event; that dated event was moved out of the schedule text. Whether adult volunteers can take part in Glissando is not stated. Committee meeting times are not published.

records.name: Minds Matter Philadelphia
records.summary: A three-year college mentoring program for high-potential high school students from low-income families in Philadelphia. Volunteer mentors meet with two students on Saturdays during the school year to help with college planning and applications.
records.what_you_do: Each mentor works in a small group with a co-mentor and two students. Mentors give social, emotional and professional support toward college, including essays and applications, across the three years.

schedule.text: Saturday mentoring sessions from 12:30 to 2 pm, throughout the school year.

first_step.how: Complete the online Volunteer Application linked from the chapter's volunteer page at mindsmatterphilly.org. Mentors must be four-year university graduates, and the chapter prefers mentors who stay for the full three years.
first_step.basis: You apply through an online form, must hold a four-year degree, and commit to Saturday sessions through the school year. The site does not describe an info session or visit before applying.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each mentor meets with a co-mentor and two students on Saturdays from 12:30 to 2 pm during the school year. Sessions cover college planning, essays, and applications. The page does not say whether there is an interview, training, or a background check.
first_visit_tips: Keep Saturday afternoons from 12:30 to 2 pm free during the school year.
Have your degree details ready for the online application.
Email info@mindsmatterphilly.org with questions before you apply.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the chapter's own volunteer and home pages. The Saturday 12:30 to 2 pm session time, the four-year degree rule and the online application now come from the chapter's own volunteer page; tier 1 took them from an Idealist listing, which is no longer cited. The tier 1 email admin@mindsmatter.org and website mindsmatter.org belong to the national organization. The chapter publishes info@mindsmatterphilly.org and mindsmatterphilly.org, so those replace them here; the P.O. Box is unchanged. Status uses the chapter's own dated item (three volunteer stories posted February 23, 2026). The national annual report from June 2026 is not counted, since it covers the national organization. The chapter describes itself as an independent 501(c)(3). Background check and training are not stated, and the chapter's partner logos are sponsors, not groups to check.

records.name: Mural Miles
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs group runs past public art around Philadelphia. The group stops at each piece to talk about it, and the runs are social, educational and open to all fitness levels.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk a monthly route past public art with a group, pausing at each piece to talk about it.

schedule.text: A monthly group run of about 4 to 5 miles, with a stop at each artwork. Dates, times and meeting spots are posted on Instagram.

cost.text: The site does not list a fee or waiver for the runs.

first_step.how: Follow the group's Instagram account for the next monthly date, route, and meeting spot. The site does not describe a sign-up form.
first_step.basis: The runs suit all fitness levels and move at a casual pace, but the group's pages do not say how to sign up, and dates are posted only on Instagram.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a casual run of about 4 to 5 miles at roughly 10 minutes a mile, with a stop at each artwork to learn about it and talk. The group stays together and regroups often. Biking the route is allowed, and dogs are welcome.
first_visit_tips: Carry only what you need, since storage at the start is not reliable.
Some runs start at a running store where you may leave items, so check the Instagram post for the spot.
The runs are meant to be social, so slow down if you are out of breath.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the running group page, the FAQ and the home page. Runs are monthly, about 4 to 5 miles, with one casual pace; dates, start times and meeting spots are posted on Instagram, which was not read because it is a lead platform. The site does not say whether there is a sign-up, a waiver, a fee, or whether children can join, and the Contact and mailing list links were not followed. The home page lists art projects and an art curation program that are outside the run record. Tier 1 cost text was replaced with level unknown, since no fee is published either way.

records.name: Neighbors Across Market
records.summary: Center City neighbors who talk about the proposed redevelopment of Market East and nearby building plans. The group hosts community meetings where people share ideas for projects that would serve everyday residents.
records.what_you_do: Come to a community meeting to share ideas and questions about Market East and nearby plans. An RSVP helps the group plan but is not required.

schedule.text: Community meetings are held from time to time. The group's website did not show a regular schedule.

cost.text: The one meeting found so far was free to attend.

first_step.how: Email the group at neighborsacrossmarket@gmail.com to ask about the next community meeting. The group's own website did not show meeting dates when it was checked.
first_step.basis: The one meeting found was free and did not require an RSVP, but the group's own site showed no schedule or sign-up, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The March 4, 2026 meeting ran from 5:30 to 7 pm at Winkel. The listing described a discussion of the proposed Market East redevelopment and how residents can speak up for their interests. Attendees were invited to share ideas for the neighborhood's future.
first_visit_tips: Check the Vox Populi Gallery events page for the latest listing.
An RSVP helps the group plan but is not required, so you can simply come.

records.notes: Tier 2 attempt, limited by the site. The group's website returned only the word home on two tries, and its /about path returned a 404, so no group-owned page could be read in this pass. Facts here come from the City RCO list (tier 1) and a Vox Populi Gallery event page for a March 4, 2026 meeting, which the single WebSearch surfaced and a fetch verified. That listing frames the group around the Market East redevelopment; the civic label from the City list is kept. No regular schedule, membership process or dues were found. The record is publishable as a real, open community group, but its first step is thin until the group's site works.

records.name: Northern Liberties Neighbors Association
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Liberty Lands, the community-owned park, and keep watch on zoning and building plans in Northern Liberties. They also run clean-ups, park music and movie nights, and walk-in office hours.
records.what_you_do: Join a committee such as Liberty Lands, Zoning or Education, help at a Sunday garden shift or a neighborhood clean-up, or bring an idea to office hours.

schedule.text: Community Office Hours on the first and second Saturdays, 10 am to noon, and third Thursdays, 5:30 to 7 pm. Garden volunteer mornings at Liberty Lands are listed on Sundays from 9 am to noon.

locations.label: NLNA Community Center
locations.address: 700 N 3rd Street, at the corner of Fairmount

cost.text: The site lists no membership dues or meeting fees. Community Center rental costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Stop by Community Office Hours to meet board members and share ideas. Or join a Sunday garden shift at Liberty Lands from 9 am to noon, or a neighborhood clean-up listed on the calendar.
first_step.basis: Office hours, general meetings and committees are open to the public and the calendar gives dates, but the site does not describe how a first-time volunteer is welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Office hours are a walk-in chance to meet board members and talk about neighborhood ideas. Committee meetings are in the evening at the Community Center; the calendar lists the Liberty Lands and Education committees at 7 to 8 pm, and the Zoning Committee can also be joined on Zoom. The site lists no fee for the garden shifts or clean-ups.
first_visit_tips: Check the calendar before you go, since times and rooms change.
Use the contact form on the website to ask about volunteer projects.

records.notes: Tier 2 read the get-involved, Community Center and calendar pages. The calendar runs into December 2026; the most recent past entry is the October 5, 2026 Zoning Committee meeting, which sets last_sign_of_life. Community Office Hours have no location on the calendar, so no place is given for them. Board of Directors meetings (Mondays, 6:30 to 7:30 pm) are listed, but the site does not say whether they are open to the public. Accessibility (wheelchair access, elevator, quiet room) is not stated on any page read. Rentals go through reservations@nlna.org, which the single email field cannot hold. Tier 1 had the Community Center address twice (as the meeting place and as the City list address); merged into one entry. The June 4, 2026 general meeting on the homepage is not used because the calendar has newer dated items. Email and contact name come from tier 1 (City list); the group's site shows no general email.

leads_only.name: Cedar Park Neighbors
leads_only.note: A neighbors group that came up in the search for Neighbors Across Market. Not checked; its own site was not read.

notes: Seven groups in batch order. 30 WebFetch calls (cap 60) and 1 WebSearch (the hard cap, now used). No 403s, bot checks or rate limits were seen; the failures were pages that returned only the word home, or a 404. Neighbors Across Market: the group's own site returned only the word home on two tries and a 404 on /about, so its record rests on the City RCO list, the tier 1 data, and a Vox Populi Gallery listing for a March 4, 2026 meeting that was verified by fetch. Two contact emails now use the group's own published general address (Logan Square: info@lsnaphilly.org; Minds Matter Philadelphia: info@mindsmatterphilly.org); the tier 1 values are recorded in each record's notes for review. Duplicate location entries were merged for the Jewish Chorale and Northern Liberties. An East Kensington neighbors association was named in a search result with no URL, so it is not listed as a lead. Group files under data/groups were read only, and nothing under data/ was edited. Verdict counts: publish 7.
